metadata.title: Finite element approximations of symmetric tensors on simplicial grids in $\mathbb{R}^n$: the lower order case

extraction_notes.note: The sentence introducing omega_F is repeated word for word in Section 5. Following 'one node per repeated statement', only the Section 4.1 copy is a node, so the finishing step's warning about the uncovered Section 5 introduction remains.
Several displayed formulas end without a period, and the next sentence starts directly after them. I split the nodes at the display's end, which leaves mid-sentence warnings on these boundaries.

Section 6 constructs the 3D face bubble spaces step by step in prose, with no algorithm environment. I extracted it as an unmarked algorithm with 11 steps; its numbered equations sit inside the steps.

K-ellipticity and the discrete B-B condition are the two conditions that standard Brezzi theory requires. I typed them as definitions (external, standard) rather than as claims or assumptions, because Theorem 4.1 is what proves they hold.
The statement that the stability of the unenriched pair cannot be established is typed open_problem; it could also be read as a remark that motivates the enrichment.

Theorem 5.1 has no proof environment. It rests on prose claims ('a similar proof of Lemma 4.2 shows', and an interpolation operator stated without proof), so it and those claims are marked semi_formal, and PP11 is the one-sentence summary that justifies it.

I did not extract the two numerical error tables of Section 7, the introduction's preview of the 18+3 / 48+6 degree-of-freedom counts (restated in Section 5 as ClP12), or the introduction's mention of Raviart-Thomas elements as the 1D member of the auxiliary family.

\section{Numerical test}

We compute a 2D pure displacement problem  on the unit square $\Omega=[0,1]^2$
     with a homogeneous boundary condition
         that $u\equiv 0$ on $\partial\Omega$.
In the computation, we let the compliance tensor in \eqref{eqn1}
   \a{
      A \sigma &= \frac 1{2\mu} \left(
       \sigma - \frac{\lambda}{2\mu + n \lambda} \operatorname{tr}(\sigma)
        \delta \right), \quad n=2,  }
  where $\delta=\p{1 &0\\0&1}$, and $\mu=1/2$ and $\lambda=1$ are the
    Lam\'e constants.
Let  the  exact solution be
   \e{\lab{e-2}   u= \p{ e^{x-y}x (1-x) y (1-y)\\
    \sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y)}. }
The true stress function $\sigma$
     and the load function $f$ are defined by the equations in
    \eqref{eqn1},   for the given  solution $u$.


In the computation, the level one grid consists of two right triangles,
   obtained by cutting the unit
   square with a north-east line.
Each grid is refined into a half-sized grid uniformly, to get
   a higher level grid.
In all the computation, the discrete systems of equations are
solved by Matlab backslash solver.

We use the bubble enriched $P_2$ symmetric stress finite element with
   $P_1$ discontinuous displacement finite element, $k=2$ in \eqref{Vh} and in
    \eqref{Sh-plus}, and $k=2$ in \eqref{Sh}.
That is, 3 $P_3$ bubbles are enriched each edge.
In Table \ref{b-2}, the errors and the convergence order
   in various norms are listed  for the true solution \eqref{e-2}.
The optimal order of convergence is observed  for both displacement and stress,
  see Table \ref{b-2}, as shown in the theorem.

As a comparison,  we also test   the Arnold--Winther element from \cite{Arnold-Winther-conforming}, which  has a same degree of freedom as ours, 21, on each  element.
